title: Reading simple sentences
examples: Teacher, how do I know when to stop reading?
Can you show me how to point when I read?
What does it mean to read for sense?

explain.say: A sentence is a group of words that makes sense. You read it one word at a time.

draw.text: Point under each word as you read

explain.say: Point under each word as you read it. Your finger helps your eyes keep their place.

draw.text: The cat sat on the mat.

explain.say: A sentence starts with a capital letter. Look at the first word. It starts with a capital T.
A sentence ends with a full stop. When you reach it, pause your voice.
When you finish, check that it makes sense. If it sounds wrong, read it again.

faq.q: Why do I have to point with my finger?
faq.a: Pointing helps your eyes stay on the right word. It helps you read each word in order.
asks: How do I keep my eyes on the words?
Should I point when I read?

faq.q: What is the difference between a capital letter and a small letter?
faq.a: A capital letter is a big letter used at the start of a sentence. A small letter is the regular letter used after the start. The first word always needs a capital letter.
asks: When do I use a big letter?

faq.q: What should I do when I see a full stop?
faq.a: When you see a full stop, pause your voice for a moment. Then read the next sentence.
asks: What sound do I make at the end?
How do I show a full stop?
Do I pause at a full stop?

faq.a: It means checking if the words you read make sense together. If the words sound silly, then the sentence does not make sense. You check if the story makes sense to you.
asks: How do I know if it makes sense?
What is the point of sense reading?
Does it have to sound right?

faq.q: If I read it wrong, what should I do?
faq.a: It is okay to read it wrong sometimes. Just stop, look back at the words, and try reading it again. You can always try again.

facts: Sentences always begin with a capital letter.
A full stop tells you to pause before the next sentence.
Finger tracking helps you follow words while reading.
Reading for sense means checking if the story makes sense.

quiz.say: Think about reading a sentence. Where does your finger point?
quiz.show: 👆 The cat sat on the mat.
quiz.why: Point under each word as you read it. Then your eyes keep their place.

wrong.0: Your finger moves along, so point under every word.
wrong.2: Your finger helps you keep your place, so point under each word.

quiz.say: Read the sentences. Tap the one that makes sense.

options.show: The bed ran to the shop.
options.say: The bed ran to the shop.

quiz.why: A dog can run fast, so this sentence makes sense.

wrong.0: A car is far too big for a dog to eat, so this sentence sounds wrong.
wrong.1: A bed stays in one place, so this sentence sounds wrong.
